checks.diagnosis: The prompt allows cuts that split a finite auxiliary/copula from its predicate, which frequently produces contradiction or loses essential predicate material.
checks.evidence: en_us_633, en_us_408, en_us_1116, en_us_936, en_us_378 — each case shows a harmful cut placed immediately after a finite auxiliary or copula (e.g. variants of 'is/was/will') so the following span contains the clause's predicate and the cut causes high contradiction or cohesion loss.
checks.type_predicate: Positions that occur immediately after a finite auxiliary or copula (a clause head that introduces the main predication) in the source sentence.

edit.text: Do not cut immediately after a finite auxiliary or copula (e.g. when the marker follows a clause head like a finite 'be' or auxiliary); such cuts split the verb from its complement and often produce contradiction or lost cohesion.

orders.diagnosis: When multiple candidate cuts fall inside the same noun phrase, the prompt prefers earlier internal splits instead of the later cut that preserves the whole NP, hurting cohesion.
orders.evidence: en_us_337, en_us_998, en_us_721 — in each sentence the measurement prefers the later cut that leaves the full noun phrase intact (keeping the NP together yields much higher H_set than cutting inside it).
orders.type_predicate: Sentences where two candidate markers occur inside the same noun phrase: one marker strictly inside the NP and another marker immediately after the NP boundary.

edit.text: When two candidates lie inside the same noun phrase, prefer the later candidate that leaves the entire NP intact (choose the marker immediately after the NP over one inside it).
